Assessment incorporating literature:
- Diagnosis of inflation pressures aligns with research showing pandemic-era supply-chain disruptions and CPI weight shifts inflated measured prices (e.g., COVID-19 Inflation Weighting in Israel, June 2022), while war-related energy and food shocks skewed the distribution of inflation outcomes to the upside, raising “inflation-at-risk” (Mixing it up: Inflation at risk, May 29, 2024). Recent work on profits/markups (The Beginning of the Trend: Interest Rates, Profits and Markups, Oct 2023) also supports the statement’s “broader price pressures.”
- The policy response—front-loaded rate hikes to 3–3.25% with continued balance-sheet reduction—is consistent with Taylor-rule and rule-like policy evaluations (Papell, Molodtsova, Nikolsko-Rzhevskyy, 2008) and the narrative evidence on credibility and expectations management (Romer and Romer). This should help anchor inflation expectations and compress the upper tail of the inflation distribution noted in the inflation-at-risk literature.
- Implementation details—raising interest on reserve balances and ON RRP—fit the modern floor-system framework discussed in Goodfriend (2002), supporting effective transmission.
Net sentiment: Cautious/hawkish. The tone remains negative due to elevated inflation and global headwinds (“tremendous human and economic hardship”), but is tempered by credible, systematic tightening aimed at restoring price stability. Adjusting for these academic insights, the negativity is less pronounced than -0.25.
